Zhinvali Reservoir

A turquoise artificial lake in the Aragvi valley — the first big view on the Georgian Military Highway.

Time needed
1 h
From Tbilisi
65 km · 1:15
Road
Paved
Car needed
Economy class
Season
May–October
Entry
free

Zhinvali is the point where the drive changes character. An hour out of Tbilisi the lowland scenery ends and a long, narrow, startlingly turquoise lake appears on the right, winding between wooded ridges. The colour is genuine, caused by fine mineral particles the Aragvi carries down from the mountains, and it is strongest under direct sun.

The reservoir was created in 1985 when the Zhinvali dam was completed. It supplies a large part of Tbilisi's drinking water and generates power at the same time. Old villages and medieval structures were flooded when the valley filled; in dry years, when the level drops sharply, fragments of walls reappear, which keeps local legends in good supply.

In practice Zhinvali is a stop rather than a destination:

  • Roadside viewpoints between the dam and Ananuri, at almost every bend
  • Ananuri fortress standing directly on the shore, so both fit into one visit
  • Seasonal boat and pedalo hire in the northern arm of the lake
  • Roadside cafés and trout restaurants south of the dam

The water level changes a lot through the year. In spring the reservoir is full and the colour is at its most intense; by late summer the shoreline is exposed and the effect is noticeably weaker.

Practical advice

Morning light or bright midday sun give the best photographs — under cloud the turquoise disappears almost completely and the water turns grey. Stop only in the marked lay-bys, because the road is narrow and standing on a bend is dangerous. Swimming near the dam is prohibited and the currents are unpredictable. Toilets and coffee are available at Ananuri and in Zhinvali village. Half an hour is plenty for the viewpoints if you are heading further north.

How to get there from Tbilisi

From Tbilisi head north on the Georgian Military Highway (E117) through Mtskheta and Natakhtari to Zhinvali — about 65 km and an hour and ten to fifteen minutes. After the dam the road follows the shoreline, and the next ten kilometres are the stretch with the views. The asphalt is good but narrow, cut into the rock, with plenty of blind corners, so overtake lorries carefully. Fill up in Natakhtari, as stations become scarce higher up. An economy car is entirely sufficient.

Nearby places

Fortress

Ananuri Fortress

A 17th-century castle on the shore of the Zhinvali reservoir — the most photogenic stop on the Georgian Military Highway.

Monastery

Svetitskhoveli Cathedral

The 11th-century cathedral of Mtskheta, said to hold the robe of Christ — the mother church of Georgian Orthodoxy.

Monastery

Jvari Monastery

A 6th-century church on a cliff above the meeting of the Aragvi and Mtkvari — the starting point of Georgian architecture.
